models.title: Reading again · Three Weeks in the Pantanal

block.label: READ AGAIN · THREE WEEKS IN THE PANTANAL
block.html:
Read the text aloud. After each paragraph, the teacher asks you to find one modal verb and say which tense the verbs are in.

Last summer, Lucas Moreira spent three weeks as a volunteer at a wildlife rescue center in the Pantanal, in the west of Brazil. The center takes care of wild animals that are hurt, sick or lost. When the animals are healthy again, the team sends them back to nature.

On his first day, Lucas was nervous. He couldn't remember all the rules, and he was worried that he might make a mistake. "You must wash your hands before and after you touch an animal," the manager, Carla, explained patiently. "And you mustn't give the animals names. They aren't pets. They have to stay wild."

Every morning, the volunteers had to wake up at 5:30. They cleaned the cages carefully, prepared the food and fed the animals. Lucas couldn't believe how much a young tapir could eat! In the afternoons, he usually helped the vet. One day, while she was checking a parrot with a broken wing, the bird bit Lucas's finger hard. "You should hold it more gently," Carla said, laughing.

The most difficult moment came in the second week. A farmer arrived with a baby anteater. It was alone, and it was very weak. The team worked quickly, but nobody knew if it could survive. For three nights, Lucas and the vet took turns feeding it every two hours. On the fourth morning, the little anteater was walking slowly around its box and looking for food. Everyone was smiling.

Today, Lucas is studying biology at university, and he wants to go back to the Pantanal next year. "You don't have to be a vet to help animals," he says. "You just have to be patient and work hard. Anyone can do it."
